newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end flat to weaker, trade dull.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end flat to weaker, trade dull.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended flat to weaker in thin, featurelss holiday week trading.

The precious metals complex largely ignored a sharp dip in November U.S. durable goods orders. U.S. Commerce Dept said orders in that month were off 1.6 percent in contrast to analysts' expectations of a modest 0.1 percent rise.
The dollar's brief surge to a 44-month high of 116.20 yen also failed to excite the torpid yellow metal market.
COMEX February gold settled unchanged at $371.10 an ounce, traded narrowly between $371.70 and $370.80.
Over-the-counter options in gold and silver expired 0930 EST, which prompted one fund to cover its short position in silver, a dealer said.
"Even after the expiry, there was some good buying interest in the silver for most of the day," the dealer added.
London bullion market reopened Friday after a two-day Christmas break, but trading was sluggish and rangebound.
Mid-afternoon New York bullion was quoted at $369.20/$369.70 an ounce, off the morning's high of above $370.00.
COMEX March silver went out 1.5 cents weaker at $4.913, after the market failed to cling on to slim initial gains from the fund and commission house buying.
Estimated volume in COMEX gold and silver were just 7,500 and 8,000 lots respectively.
NYMEX platinum was able to shake off the morning's losses to end unchanged at $375.10 an ounce in the most-active April contract.
But NYMEX March palladium failed to capture some of platinum's momentum and ended 65 cents lower at $118.75 an ounce.
